story.title: Our story begins with a river
story.paragraph1: Abuela Ecológica Foundation was born in the Northern Zone of Costa Rica, on the banks of a river that was losing its forest.
story.paragraph2: At 80 years old, Mrs. Bertalia González decided not to stand by. She began germinating seeds at home and reforesting the riverbanks with native species where life had once flourished.
story.paragraph3: She did not do it for recognition. She did it for the animals, for the land, and for those who had not yet been born.
story.quote: “We must plant trees to leave life for the children who have not yet been born.”
story.closing: For San Carlos, Costa Rica and the world.

aboutStory.title: The Ecological Grandmother
aboutStory.p1: The Abuela Ecologica Foundation was born inspired by the legacy of Bertalia González Villalobos (1935–2020), a community leader in reforestation and water protection.
aboutStory.p2: With seeds in her hands and conviction in her heart, she traveled through communities planting trees as an act of intergenerational responsibility.
aboutStory.p3: In 2018, together with her daughter Laura Alfaro González and her granddaughter María Murillo Alfaro, that legacy became a foundation.

arboles-plumas.title: Trees and Feathers
arboles-plumas.summary: Restoring forests to give the Great Green Macaw a home again
arboles-plumas.description: Restoring the Great Green Macaw's habitat in San Carlos by planting key tree species and strengthening biological corridors.
content: Trees and Feathers (Árboles y Plumas) is a project dedicated to restoring the habitat of the Great Green Macaw. One of Costa Rica's most iconic macaws, this species is also among its most threatened. Deforestation and forest fragmentation have drastically reduced its habitat, leaving it confined to small, isolated populations.

San Carlos remains a key area for its recovery. Forests, committed communities, and essential tree species such as the mountain almond still exist here, offering the conditions needed for the macaw to feed and nest once again.

Trees and Feathers was created as a direct response to this challenge: restoring biological corridors through the planting of key tree species and the active participation of local communities, institutions, and strategic partners.

bosque-los-lolos.title: Los Lolos Forest
bosque-los-lolos.summary: Ecological restoration to strengthen connectivity between forests and protect water sources.
bosque-los-lolos.description: Restoration of 1,400 m² of land through the planting of 700 native trees to protect two springs of strategic importance to Costa Rica's Northern Region.
content: The Los Lolos Forest project involved restoring a former pasture of approximately 1,400 square meters in San Vicente, Ciudad Quesada. The area is home to two springs of great importance to local communities: one is part of Ciudad Quesada's water supply system, while the other provides water to the community of El Porvenir.

Planting 700 native trees helps protect these water sources, improves water infiltration and regulation in the soil, and strengthens ecological connectivity between nearby forest fragments, creating more favorable conditions for regional biodiversity.

The initiative received technical support from professionals at the School of Forest Engineering and the School of Agronomy of the Costa Rica Institute of Technology (TEC), who provided guidance throughout the planning, species selection, and restoration establishment stages.

Since the site is located approximately 1,400 meters above sea level, native species adapted to the area's climatic, soil, and ecological conditions were carefully selected to maximize tree survival and ensure a lasting environmental impact.

nietos-abuela-ecologica.title: Grandchildren of the Ecological Grandma
nietos-abuela-ecologica.summary: Bringing joy and hope to children in vulnerable rural communities.
nietos-abuela-ecologica.description: A support program for children in vulnerable rural communities, promoting their overall development and connection with nature.
content: Grandchildren of the Ecological Grandma is a charitable campaign launched in 2020 with a simple yet meaningful purpose: to bring a Christmas gift to children living in vulnerable rural communities in Costa Rica's Northern Region.

Since its beginning, the campaign has delivered more than 1,700 gifts thanks to the support of sponsors, generous donations, and companies that believe in the social impact of this initiative. Each gift represents much more than an object: it is a gesture of support, joy, and dignity for the families who receive it.
Over the years, the campaign has reached several communities:
• 2020: 350 gifts delivered in the Maleku Indigenous Territory, in the El Sol, Margarita, and Tonjibe settlements.
• 2021: Around 500 gifts delivered in Santa Rosa de Pocosol and Tres y Tres de Pocosol, as well as to CENCINAI beneficiaries in San Joaquín de Cutris and Dulce Nombre de Ciudad Quesada.
• 2022: 150 gifts delivered in Boca San Carlos.
• 2023: Nearly 350 gifts for children attending CENCINAI centers in Boca Tapada, Santa Rita, Boca San Carlos, and Cureñita, as well as the Pediatric Unit of San Carlos Hospital.
• 2024: 350 gifts delivered in Boca Tapada, Santa Rita, Boca San Carlos, and Cureñita.
• 2025: 200 gifts distributed in Crucitas and Moravia de Cutris, the Pediatric Unit of San Carlos Hospital, and the Hogarcito in Ciudad Quesada.

Since its inception, the campaign has been coordinated by María Fernanda Murillo and sustained through the ongoing commitment of individuals and organizations that choose each year to participate as sponsors or make donations.
Grandchildren of the Ecological Grandma shows that solidarity can also transform territories, build community, and leave a lasting mark on childhood.

cta.title: Help bring a smile to children across the Northern Region
cta.text: Your donation supports the purchase of gifts, delivery logistics, and the continuation of this charitable campaign.

reforestacion-consciente.title: Conscious Reforestation
reforestacion-consciente.summary: Planting native trees to protect water springs and strengthen ecosystems in La Tigra, San Carlos.
reforestacion-consciente.description: A reforestation project that combines native tree planting with environmental education to protect water springs and strengthen ecosystems in La Tigra, San Carlos.
content: During October, November, and December 2020, several reforestation activities took place in the La Tigra area of San Carlos, resulting in the successful planting of 5,000 trees from 55 native species.

One of the restored properties borders the Children's Eternal Rainforest, while the other belongs to the ASADA La Lucha – La Vega, a local community water association. Both properties contain springs of significant ecological value.
The property belonging to the ASADA contains water intakes that supply more than 5,000 families, making the reforestation effort directly relevant to protecting this vital water resource.
During the activities, volunteers learned about forest species and wildlife and had the opportunity to observe snakes, frogs, birds, and mammals in their natural habitats.
This project was carried out as part of an environmental compensation initiative funded by a private company, with our organization responsible for its full implementation.

un-norte-lapa-verde.title: A Future for the Great Green Macaw
un-norte-lapa-verde.summary: An ecological restoration project focused on donating and planting mountain almond trees to protect the Great Green Macaw's habitat.
un-norte-lapa-verde.description: An ecological restoration project that aims to protect the Great Green Macaw's habitat through mountain almond tree planting and the active participation of local communities.
un-norte-lapa-verde.location: Huetar Norte Region and Atlantic Slope
content: A Future for the Great Green Macaw is a conservation project carried out between November 2019 and July 2020, focused on strengthening the habitat of one of Costa Rica's most iconic and threatened species: the Great Green Macaw.

The Great Green Macaw is classified as Endangered by the IUCN and under Costa Rican national legislation. Its main threat remains habitat loss, particularly the disappearance of the mountain almond tree, on which it directly depends for food and nesting sites.

Several studies have shown that between 80% and 90% of the Great Green Macaw's diet consists of mountain almond fruit, and that approximately 90% of its nests are located in natural cavities in these trees. Its survival is literally linked to the presence of mountain almond trees in the landscape.

In response to this situation, the project focused on donating and planting 5,000 mountain almond trees throughout the Huetar Norte Region and the Atlantic Slope, areas that form part of the species' historical range.

The project brought together environmental communication activities, the development of educational materials, seedling propagation, and technical support for beneficiaries, encouraging the care and monitoring of the planted trees.

The seeds used were collected in strategic locations such as Veracruz, El Sahino de Pital, Santa Clara, La Tigra, and Peñas Blancas. The project also received support from the ICE nursery in Sarapiquí, which donated 4,000 seedlings.

A Future for the Great Green Macaw laid the groundwork for future ecological restoration projects by Fundación Abuela Ecológica, establishing a conservation model based on science, local territories, and community participation.

inclusion-intercultural.title: Intercultural Inclusion
inclusion-intercultural.summary: A socio-environmental project bringing together reforestation, environmental education, and the inclusion of Indigenous communities in the Northern Region.
inclusion-intercultural.description: An intercultural inclusion project that promotes reforestation as a space for connection, environmental education, and stronger social ties between Indigenous communities and the wider population.
content: Intercultural Inclusion was created with the purpose of protecting nature through reforestation, using this activity as an opportunity for connection between Indigenous communities and residents of Costa Rica's Northern Region.
The project combines environmental action with social and cultural education, promoting respect, inclusion, and mutual learning among people from different backgrounds, age groups, and institutions.
Reforestation serves as a common thread, helping to raise environmental awareness, strengthen community relationships, and create opportunities for intercultural dialogue.
The first edition of the project took place on October 30, 2019, with approximately 110 participants and representatives from the Boruca, Ngöbe, and Maleku Indigenous peoples.
The event also received support from several public institutions, social organizations, and community groups, bringing together a collective experience of significant social and environmental value.
This project is envisioned as a driving force for future initiatives that promote more inclusive and sustainable development, not only in the Northern Region but throughout the country.
